name: Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

podcast.body: Released on June 1, 1967, this album marked a significant shift in music, moving beyond "kiddie music" and the simple rock and roll sound. Its sophistication elevated music to an art form, contributing to the broader acceptance of rock as a serious genre. "The biggest change came on June 1, 1967, when the Beatles released Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This "legendary" album finally secured the Album of the Year Grammy for The Beatles in 1968, after they had lost twice to Frank Sinatra. Described as the Beatles' "bid for adult respectability," it was also seminal in the "shift of pop promotion from singles to albums" and seemed to bring the Grammys "somewhat up to date." "It figures that the Beatles bid for adult respectability, the legendary Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club band, finally took album of the Year."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Pseudonymous Release
podcast.body: This album was released on June 1, 1967, and was credited to Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, a pseudonym for The Beatles. For this record, The Beatles consciously assumed the role of this fake band, although they did not try very hard to conceal their true identity, making it "the world's worst secret" when it came to band pseudonyms. "But for that record, The Beatles assumed the role of this fake band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
